title: Antonelli fastest but Verstappen on pole in Las Vegas
extract: Kimi Antonelli set the quickest qualifying time but a five-place penalty drops him to sixth, leaving Max Verstappen on pole alongside George Russell; McLaren's Lando Norris starts third and both Ferrari drivers missed the top-ten shootout.

title: F1 agrees framework for switch to V8 engines from 2030, says FIA
extract: Formula One stakeholders have unanimously backed a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 framework for 2030, with limited hybridisation and advanced sustainable fuels aimed at simpler, lighter cars and more attack-oriented racing.

title: Intel Linux NPU Driver 1.39.1 Released With Nova Lake Support
extract: Intel's user-space Linux NPU Driver 1.39.1 adds official support for Nova Lake's sixth-generation NPU IP, complementing the mainlined IVPU kernel driver; the release recommends OpenVINO 2026.5.

title: Debian 13.8 Released With 150+ Security Updates
extract: Debian 13.8 refreshes Trixie installation media with more than 150 security advisories covered, alongside package rebuilds, bug fixes and compatibility updates involving KWin, OpenSSL, glibc and Thunderbird.

title: FreeBSD 15.2 Beta 3 Released Following 17 Security Advisories
extract: The third 15.2 beta folds in fixes for 17 newly disclosed advisories, updated OpenZFS and other system fixes; the advisories include privilege escalation and a remote-code-execution issue in the NFSv4 server.

title: GnuPG's GPGME Affected By Critical Security Bug In Turn Affecting Mail Clients, Flatpak
extract: A crafted, very long OpenPGP user ID can trigger a double-free in GPGME, potentially exposing application data and possibly enabling remote code execution; maintainer Werner Koch urges affected users to update immediately.

title: Intel Preps Linux 7.5 Change To Better Handle Multiple GPUs With Lots Of VRAM
extract: A Linux 7.5 DRM change expands GEM/TTM buffer-object mmap ranges from 1TB to 8TB, addressing address-space exhaustion in multi-GPU systems with very large VRAM, including future Intel D-series accelerators.

title: AMD Contributes Integration For Content-Adaptive / Adaptive Backlight Modulation To GNOME
extract: AMD's Mutter integration exposes Adaptive Backlight Modulation through GNOME's compositor, allowing compatible Ryzen AI laptop panels to reduce backlight power dynamically based on screen content, with some trade-off in colour accuracy.

title: System76 Thelio Prime: A Petite But Performant AMD-Powered Linux PC
extract: Phoronix tests the redesigned 9.78-litre Linux desktop, built in-house from aluminium and steel and configurable up to Ryzen 9 9900X, discrete Radeon or GeForce graphics, 96GB RAM and 16TB NVMe; the review finds it well engineered and quiet under load.

title: Fedora Incident Response Policy Drafted For Improving Workflow & Security Disclosures
extract: Fedora's Security SIG has drafted an incident-response policy defining what constitutes an incident, how it is declared, how embargoed information is handled and how communication should work, partly addressing lessons from the XZ Utils crisis.

title: AMDXDNA Driver Reaches Version 1.0, Ryzen AI NPU10 & NPU11 Coming To Linux 7.5
extract: The in-tree AMDXDNA driver is reaching version 1.0 with Linux 7.5 and prepares support for AIE4-based Ryzen AI NPU10/NPU11; recent user-space work has made Ryzen AI NPUs increasingly useful for local LLM workloads on Linux.

title: Rust Coreutils 0.13 Release Delivers More Performance, Better Compatibility
extract: The Rust reimplementation of GNU Coreutils reports gains such as basenc base58 around 35 times faster and cut 23% faster, while reaching 95.26% of the GNU Test Suite and improving file handling and Windows compatibility.

title: Vulkan 1.4.369 Introduces New AMD Extension For Improving Ray-Tracing Performance
extract: Vulkan 1.4.369 adds experimental VK_AMDX_multi_level_acceleration_structure, allowing deeper instance hierarchies for ray-traced scenes to improve update granularity, reuse geometry and potentially reduce acceleration-structure memory use.

title: Cloud Hypervisor 55 Released With AArch64 Nested Virtualization, Up To 990 ARM vCPUs
extract: The Rust-based virtual-machine monitor adds AArch64 nested virtualization for FEAT_NV2-capable systems, raises the KVM ARM vCPU ceiling from 255 to 990 and includes security hardening, VFIO DMA-BUF support and live-migration improvements.

title: Kwi Sees First Release As KDE's New Terminal Emulator
extract: KDE's new Kwi terminal emulator reaches 0.1, built on Ghostty and now an official KDE application; the first release brings tab, global-menu and theming improvements, with source and Flatpak builds available.

title: FFmpeg 9.1 Released With NVIDIA Optical Flow FRUC, APV Vulkan Encoder
extract: FFmpeg 9.1 adds NVIDIA optical-flow frame-rate up-conversion, a Vulkan encoder for the royalty-free APV codec, ASTC image support, an improved AAC encoder and a broad set of codec, filter and device enhancements.

title: Linux 7.5 To Optionally Block /proc/kcore Access For Better Security
extract: A queued Linux 7.5 patch adds a boot-time kcore=off option to disable /proc/kcore, reducing exposure of physical-memory and kernel-address-space dumps on systems that do not need the facility.

title: LLVM Effectively Completes Its Relicensing After Nearly A Decade Of Work
extract: LLVM's long-running effort to move historic contributions to Apache 2.0 with LLVM exceptions is effectively complete: more than 99.5% of code is now covered, following agreements with over 1,300 contributors and about 100 organisations.

title: MorphOS: Bluetooth stack MBlue 1.0
extract: MorphOS 3.21 gains a native Bluetooth stack with support for keyboards, mice, AHI audio devices, headset microphones, phone file transfers and battery reporting, including support for selected USB dongles and built-in Bluetooth on G5 Macs.

title: AmigaOS 4: PuTTY 1.0
extract: A new native AmigaOS 4 port of PuTTY 0.85 brings SSH, Telnet, remote login and serial connectivity, with SFTP/SCP, Unicode support and a ReAction interface.

title: Code editor for AmigaOS 4 and MorphOS: Pragtical 3.12.5
extract: The Pragtical code editor port for AmigaOS 4 and MorphOS reaches 3.12.5, adding code folding and fixing a stack crash on AmigaOS 4.1 caused by an undersized stack-cookie setting.

title: Football game: Final demo version of Mundialito 3
extract: The final demo of this AMOS Pro football game for Amiga 1200 rewrites player movement and set-piece routines, adds ten teams per league, improves the AI and league economy, and completes its intro music and menus.

title: Program for testing block devices: Devtest 2.0
extract: Devtest 2.0 improves an Amiga utility that tests block-device drivers and physical drives, adding better support for disks larger than 4GB and more accurate benchmarks.

title: BASIC-Cross-Compiler: QBAVision 1.4
extract: QBAVision combines a BASIC development environment with a Motorola 68000 cross-compiler for native AmigaOS Hunk programmes; updates add improved AmigaOS 1.3 presentation and speech, graphics tools and a native Windows IDE.

title: Classic in HD: Another World - 20th Anniversary Edition (AGA/RTG)
extract: A new AGA/RTG Amiga port of the 20th Anniversary Edition uses the open-source RAWGL engine, optimizing HD backgrounds while rendering the original polygon-based moving objects in HD across hardware from a standard A1200 to faster accelerator and emulator setups.

title: Science-Fiction strategy: Mass Fraction
extract: This new hard-science-fiction economic strategy game for Amiga A1200 tasks players with building a space company capable of creating and staffing an orbital station; it is available free or by donation and was made with AI assistance.

title: Light in the dark: 20 long books for short winter days
extract: A curated list of 20 ambitious long novels includes Dhalgren, Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, William T Vollmann's Cold War/CIA epic A Table for Fortune and China Miéville's occult-military The Rouse, spanning science fiction, fantasy, espionage and weird fiction.

title: The best recent crime and thrillers – review roundup
extract: The Guardian's latest crime and thriller roundup covers Nick Harkaway's new George Smiley continuation, Mick Herron's Slow Horses novellas, a psychological thriller and two historical mysteries, with Cold War espionage, MI5 intrigue and wartime Portmeirion in the mix.

title: Blade Runner 2099: fans will have no idea what is happening in this sci-fi sequel. Why is it even on TV?
extract: The Guardian's review of Prime Video's Blade Runner sequel series finds the Philip K. Dick-inspired dystopia visually atmospheric but narratively opaque, with Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh leading a story set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049.

title: Bill’s Included review – Rob Brydon’s new character is as glorious as Gavin & Stacey’s Uncle Bryn
extract: Rob Brydon's new BBC sitcom casts him as a recently divorced landlord renting rooms to four students; the Guardian praises Brydon's gloriously awkward comic performance while finding the ensemble and storylines thin.

title: The Slightest Touch to California Schemin’: the seven best films to watch on TV this week
extract: The Guardian's weekly film picks include James McAvoy's California Schemin', a true-story comedy about Dundee rappers posing as Americans, alongside Cabaret, Downhill Racer and the documentary The Slightest Touch.

title: Steps review – Netflix’s Disney-lite Cinderella rework has enough pep in its step
extract: Netflix's animated Cinderella rework follows the misunderstood stepsisters Lilith and Margot on a magical quest; the review finds the plot crowded but the film lively, funny and more enjoyable than much of the streamer's recent animation.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth review – Tarantino and Fincher join forces for Brad Pitt’s glorious return
extract: David Fincher directs Quentin Tarantino's sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, returning Brad Pitt as Cliff Booth in a 1977 Los Angeles crime caper; the Guardian highlights its black comedy, outrageous energy and Pitt's comic performance.
